title: Business software is next
storyboard: preview/films/business-software-next/boards/talk/board.js (44 stills, approved by Ruben on 29 Oct 2026: "let's generate it")
structure: Body: a storyboard wall (Ruben's notes, 30 Oct 2026): 37 cards in six rows (intro, 01, 02, 03, 04, close) as a snake; the camera glides card to card and pulls back between rows past the chapter header on the wall; each card's resting frame is its approved still
Built on Nextcloud: _lib/scenes/closing.js builtOnScene, lead buildiq, English, never voiced
Install board: _lib/scenes/closing.js installScene, English, never voiced
timing: voice/takes.json ({ id: { file, dur, words, wer } }) on every load: the camera holds on a card for 0.35 s + its take + 0.45 s, rounded up to the next beat; a 1.64 s glide within a row; a row change of at least ROW_OUT + ROW_IN with the section take (section-01 to section-04) as voice-over; without a take, words / 2.6 per second (at least 3 s). The wall ends on a bar line.

brand_rules: BIBLE: one orange per scene, solid fills, pointy-top hexes that flip in and never rotate, no bounce or overshoot, depth by opacity
BIBLE round 30: the opening and closing pieces are never voiced; music ducks 15 dB under the voice (film.music.duckDb 15)
BIBLE round 31: the version without voice-over keeps every written word
music: score.mjs house bed in D, one four-chord progression per act, pad throughout, offbeat bass from bar 5, kick and hat in the build acts (precedent, the math, trust, the store)
deviations: English only (film.langs = ['en']); the on-screen strings live in the storyboard acts, not in a { nl, en } table
No-voice captions on two scenes whose spoken point is not on screen: core-vs-ecosystem and gates-quote
director_notes_2026_10_30: One viewer, not a room: who-codes 'Do you write code?' with one orange cell (you); who-patched 'Did you patch something last week?'; fun-week 'How was your week?' then a hard cut within the card to 'Mine sucked.' on the spoken word; title words 'Not everyone writes code. But almost everyone knows exactly what software they need. Business software is next.'
Storyboard wall instead of hard cuts: flat cards on a cobalt-900 wall, dimmed by opacity when the camera is not on them; no rotation, bounce, gradients or shadows

Chapter slides are written on the wall at the start of each row (number in orange mono, title, the section's line); the section boards are no longer cards but stay in the storyboard as the source of the header text
